allowed.internal/console/pi: runs the agent console's container with an interactive terminal
allowed.internal/deploy/docker: the docker CLI: which daemon a command talks to, and the build environment it must not inherit
allowed.internal/execution: the generic process runner: process groups, timeouts, the environment, streamed and bounded output, and the docker runs it places work in
allowed.internal/gitexec: git: gitexec.Command is the one constructor for every git the repository starts by name (and tar, to unpack a commit's tree)
allowed.internal/worker: the execution host: runs the tasks, checks and sessions an AppTown sends it

git.why: gitexec.Command, the one constructor every git the repository starts by name builds on; inside the allowed packages too

cmd/apptown.why: apptown dev runs the person's docker client (compose, and dev up's static-site builds) on their terminal with their whole environment, their Buildx builder included (docker.CLI drops it, as AppTown's own builds must), from one place, dockerCLI; dev_test runs compose config in a project folder, as dev up does

cmd/apptown-check.why: the checklist completer gives the prompt to the person's command on stdin and passes its stderr to their terminal; execution.Runner takes no stdin and merges the streams

cmd/apptown-worker.why: the -docker test starts the built apptown-worker as a server with a PATH holding only the fake docker, and stops it by its pid

cmd/apptownd.why: the SIGTERM test runs this test binary as a child and signals it

internal/console.why: toolchain_test reads the command's stdout and stderr apart, with a PATH of its own first; execution.Runner merges them

internal/console/consoletest.why: the fake runtime's Script streams a script's stdout alone to the caller, as the real runtime's container does; execution.Runner merges stderr into it

internal/apptown.why: inference_pi_test runs the pinned Pi SDK with exactly PATH, HOME and its own variables, so no ambient provider key reaches it; execution.Runner passes the process's environment through

internal/apptown/jobs.why: the River crash test starts this test binary as a child, reads its progress as it streams and kills it mid-job: a process it holds, which no owner's interface hands back

internal/apptown/workflowexec.why: reconcile_guidance_test runs the chat's catch-up command with only the variables it names (no HOME, so no personal git config); execution.Runner would add the process's environment

internal/worker/workertest.why: StartOnHost runs apptown-worker as a long-lived process on this machine and stops and restarts it by its pid

scripts.why: lint-check runs golangci-lint and reads its report: a gate's own program starting the tool it checks
